prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for every Atlanta homeowner — the right contractor depends on your exact location, home size, budget, preferred equipment and service expectations. I can’t look up live reviews for you here, but I can tell you how to find the best local company and what to require so you get a safe, efficient AC replacement.

Quick plan
1. Get at least 3 written estimates from reputable local contractors.
2. Require a Manual J load calculation and an AHRI-matched equipment selection.
3. Compare price, scope, warranties, and included services — not just the lowest bid.
4. Verify license, insurance, NATE certification, and recent customer reviews (Google/Yelp/BBB/Angi/Nextdoor).
5. Ask about permitting and whether the contractor will pull the permit and do code‑required inspections.

What to look for in a contractor
- Licensed and insured in Georgia. (Ask for license number and verify with local authorities.)
- NATE-certified technicians.
- Provides a Manual J (sizing), Manual S (equipment selection) and Manual D (ductwork) if ductwork is changed.
- Will pull permits and follow local code.
- Offers a written proposal with model numbers, SEER rating, total cost, labor warranty, and parts warranty.
- Offers an installation warranty and honors manufacturer labor warranty/registration.
- Uses certified refrigerant recovery and follows EPA guidelines.
- Positive recent reviews and verifiable references.

Questions to ask each company
- Are you licensed/insured? What’s your license number?
- Can you provide references from recent AC replacements in my neighborhood?
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation before selecting equipment?
- Which brand/models do you recommend and why? Can you provide AHRI match docs?
- What is included (new thermostat, pads, refrigerant, duct sealing, startup)?
- Will you pull permits and arrange inspections?
- What warranties are included (parts/labor/heat exchanger)?
- Do you offer financing and are there local utility rebates?
- Who will service the unit after installation and what is the response time for emergencies?

Red flags
- No load calculation, only “rule of thumb” sizing.
- Very low “bait” price that changes after a long list of add-ons.
- No written contract or vague scope of work.
- Contractor won’t pull permits or provide proof of insurance.
- Pressure to sign immediately or push a particular brand without explanation.

Where to find reputable Atlanta contractors
- Google/Google Maps ratings + recent review content
- Yelp and Angi reviews
- Better Business Bureau listing and complaint history
- Nextdoor for neighborhood referrals
- Local utility (Georgia Power) or state energy efficiency programs for rebates and preferred contractor lists

If you want, I can:
- Narrow this to a short list of top-rated contractors near you if you give your ZIP code;
- Review and compare 2–3 written estimates side-by-side (paste them here);
- Provide a checklist/contract template to use when evaluating bids.

Tell me your ZIP code or paste the estimates and I’ll help you from there.
